answer: A proposed coastal relay market admits one paid key per exclusive reef radio channel, proven by a signed regulator lease. At nadir tide, independent shore receivers issue simultaneous random challenges and triangulate each transmitter; a fable of a second site fails their signal logs. Validators deny pay for absent, colliding or replayed replies. A farm can share its model and rent radios, but each added key needs a separate live transmitter and lease in the same 24-channel cell; borrowing money cannot make one channel serve two keys at once.
